entities.name: Pharasmanes III of Iberia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pharasmanes III of Iberia (pharasmanes-iii-of-iberia) was a king (mepe) of Iberia who ruled from 135–185 AD, contemporaneously with the Roman emperor Antoninus Pius (138–161).


 Pharasmanes III of Iberia (pharasmanes-iii-of-iberia) ruled Iberia, a region encompassing modern-day Georgia and parts of Turkey, Azerbaijan, and Armenia, contributing to the cultural exchange between the ancient civilizations of the Caucasus and the Mediterranean.


 Pharasmanes III of Iberia (pharasmanes-iii-of-iberia) was succeeded by his son, Parthamasarvan I (pharasmanes-iii-of-iberia's Successor), who went on to expand the Iberian Kingdom's influence in the region.


 Pharasmanes III of Iberia (pharasmanes-iii-of-iberia) is notable for his diplomatic efforts with the Roman Empire, as evidenced by the presence of Roman coins and artifacts in Iberian archaeological sites.
